newsitem.title: FRANCE: BASF French revenues slip in nine months.
newsitem.headline: BASF French revenues slip in nine months.

text.p: BASF France said on Friday price pressure in the market for synthetic materials and chemicals has led to a slip in its overall divisional revenues for the year so far.
Philippe Bonnard, head of the French division of the German group, told Reuters that turnover for the first nine months of the year had slipped some two percent to 5.018 billion francs.
Revenues from synthetic materials in France had fallen 15 percent to 1.2 billion francs while its turnover from chemicals had slumped 10 percent to 1.13 billion francs, he said.
The division's agricultural product revenues had meanwhile been boosted by growing French demand for pesticides, with turnover rising some 20 percent to 1.70 billion francs.
Bonnard said BASF now had around an 11 percent share of the French pesticides market, making it the fifth largest provider.
France is overall BASF's third largest market after German and the United States.
